svg.text: How typed decision engines work: real Jev vs open verdict-2.0 vs this repo
Public-contract facts only. Proprietary internals are marked unknown — not guessed.
A · TYPESAFE JEV (THE REAL THING — CLOSED SOURCE)
Your app → typed request (state + Choice / Score / Noul schemas) → █ black box █ → probabilities + confidence
Known publicly: the typed interface idea — decisions as distributions, not prose. ~150M params, ~140 ms/decision
(timings as cataloged in openJev-verdict-2.0's benchmark table).
Unknown (proprietary): architecture, weights, training data, calibration method. Any diagram claiming
otherwise is fiction. This is exactly why open reimplementations exist.
B · OPENJEV-VERDICT-2.0 (OPEN — FROM THEIR README + RUNBOOK)
1 · Pack: [CLS] <type> <question> [SEP] [MASK]opt₀ [MASK]opt₁ … [SEP] <state> [SEP]
2 · Encode once: ModernBERT-base 149.6M (+ GLiClass NLI framing, “It is {description}”)
3 · Marker-pointer logits per option → split into TWO heads:
Distribution head → soft probs (Brier 0.064) · Confidence MLP head → P(correct) (ECE 1.4%)
4 · Per-cardinality temperature scaling (auto-loaded calibrator.json)
5 · Selective gate: high confidence → act · low → human · out-of-scope → __insufficient_evidence__
6 · Ship: Hugging Face weights → ONNX → WebGPU in-browser (<600 MB, <35 ms, zero exfiltration)
Trained: symmetric Permutation-KL (option-order bias 7.4% → 4.8%) · 8.8 h on a GTX 1660 Ti · 77.1% top-1,
2,000 held-out enterprise decisions · contamination audits · failure gallery · 9 experiment receipts.
Credit: Heman10x-NGU/openJev-verdict-2.0 (Apache-2.0). Numbers as they report them; receipts in their repo.
C · THIS REPO — OPENJEV (THE DEPLOYABLE ENVELOPE)
Same typed envelope (FastAPI + CLI + TS SDK): state + Choice / Score / Noul → probs + abstention + trace
Backends plug in like cartridges: local lexical (0.07 ms) · research byte scorer + T (0.09 ms) ·
remote · hosted. Any scorer — including a verdict-style transformer — can live behind it.
Relationship: this repo is the socket, verdict-2.0 is the strongest open bulb. Methods ported: temperature
scaling, selective curves, latency receipts, docs-fresh tests, failure gallery. Model gap remains: byte
histograms (75% toy) vs 150M transformer (77.1% enterprise) — no equivalence claimed, ever.
D · LAYA (OPEN, PUBLISHED PACKAGE — FROM THEIR README + BENCHMARKS.md)
Script/language Router → 1 of 3 checkpoints (421M English · 322M multilingual · 421M typed-decisions)
Single forward pass (~33 ms) → Choice / Score / Noul + per-(type, k) temperatures + presets + shortlist
76.6% top-1 typed-decisions · 45/51 languages usable · PyPI + HF Space · honest-limits section.
Credit: NandhaKishorM/laya (Apache-2.0). Ported here: presets, shortlist, email/lang utils, grouped temps.
Not ported: the 421M weights themselves — different league, different hardware.
